title: Plowman v. Philadelphia Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained on both issues. Issue 1 sustained: Philadelphia Presbytery erred under BCO 42-2 by not accepting Plowman's July 31, 2002 appeal; she had submitted to regular trial, so the appeal was in order and was remanded to Presbytery for adjudication. Issue 2 sustained: Presbytery erred under BCO 43-1 in finding her October 19, 2002 complaint untimely because, once the pending appeal was renamed as a complaint on Presbytery's advice, the complaint was timely. Relief: remand to Philadelphia Presbytery to hear the appeal as originally filed. The SJC also noted that under BCO 42-6 the appeal suspended the lower court's judgment and the Lord's Table censure pending final adjudication.
first_summary: A church session suspended a member from the Lord's Table and later found her guilty of contumacy. Philadelphia Presbytery refused to accept her appeal and denied her complaint as untimely. The SJC sustained her complaint, held her appeal in order because she had submitted to regular trial, and remanded for Presbytery to adjudicate the appeal.
summary: A church session suspended a member from the Lord's Table and found her guilty of contumacy. Philadelphia Presbytery's committee advised her appeal was out of order, then ruled her complaint untimely. The SJC sustained her complaint: she had submitted to regular trial, making her appeal in order under BCO 42-2, and her complaint was timely after Presbytery's advice caused the appeal to be renamed. It remanded for Presbytery to adjudicate the appeal. Filing the appeal suspended the Lord's Table censure pending final adjudication; the SJC questioned the contumacy ruling.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2002-5 (Refiled), Complaint of Nancy J. Plowman vs. Philadelphia Presbytery, lines 14, 184–190. Report by TE Dominic Aquila, with concurrence of RE Frank Brock and TE Charles McGowan; adopted 18 concurring, 0 dissenting, 1 disqualified, 1 recused, and 3 absent; approved by the full SJC on October 16, 2003. Source: cases/ga32_2004__2002-05.md, SHA256 a8648bee51c2bc9d1f8070aeba3c0bfb56ca0b198b9c7a8f2fab0b13b3e3b2d5.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 18–54, 58–60. The Session of Lehigh Valley Presbyterian Church suspended Plowman from the Sacraments on December 21, 2001 and later found her guilty of contumacy on July 1, 2002. She filed an appeal on July 31, 2002; Philadelphia Presbytery's Judicial Business Committee chairman told her it was out of order. She then filed a complaint on August 18, 2002. Presbytery denied the complaint on January 18, 2003 as untimely. The SJC framed issues under BCO 42-2 and BCO 43-1.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Judgment lines 62–66: both issues answered Yes; the appeal was remanded to Philadelphia Presbytery to be heard as originally filed. Reasoning lines 72–167: Plowman submitted to regular trial by heeding citations and attending sessions; the Session's act of ending the trial did not negate her appeal right under BCO 42-2. The Judicial Business Committee chairman acted without full committee or Presbytery authority, and a committee cannot conclude a matter under BCO 15-1. The complaint was timely under BCO 43-1 once the appeal was renamed. Lines 179–182 note BCO 42-6's suspension of judgment and censure pending final adjudication.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 169–175: the SJC said it was not persuaded that the Session properly interpreted and applied BCO 32-6.b and BCO 33-2 and noted questions about quorum and teaching elder presence; these were additional concerns, not a final merits adjudication of the contumacy charge. Concurring opinion lines 192–216 concurs in result but relies on equity, fair play, and estoppel because Presbytery's incorrect advice caused Plowman to withdraw her timely appeal and file an untimely complaint. The concurrence is not the majority's adopted reasoning.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Footnote line 40 and refiling notes lines 32 and 54: the earlier Case 2002-5 was found administratively out of order by the SJC because the matter was still before the Session. No separate incorporated decision text is supplied. The Record of the Case (ROC) and lower-court minutes are cited in the source but are not included.
